summary: The note describes the Kingdom of Gera, one of the kingdoms of the Gibe region of Ethiopia that existed from 1835 to 1887. It bordered the Kingdom of Gumma to the north, the Kingdom of Gomma to the east, and was separated from the Kingdom of Kaffa to the south by the Gojeb River. Its capital was Chala (Cira), and its territory roughly matches the modern Gera woreda.
one_line: The Kingdom of Gera, a 19th-century Gibe-region kingdom in Ethiopia (1835–1887) with its capital at Chala.
key_facts: The Kingdom of Gera existed from 1835 to 1887.
The Kingdom of Gera was one of the kingdoms in the Gibe region of Ethiopia.
The Kingdom of Gera emerged in the late 19th century.
The Kingdom of Gera shared its northern border with the Kingdom of Gumma.
The Kingdom of Gera shared its eastern border with the Kingdom of Gomma.
The Kingdom of Gera was separated from the Kingdom of Kaffa to the south by the Gojeb River.
The capital of the Kingdom of Gera was at Chala, also called Cira.
The territory of the Kingdom of Gera corresponds approximately with the modern woreda of Gera.
